subject: Request: mid-cycle capacity top-up and billing accelerator
messages:

Cc: procurement <procurement@clearviewhealth.com>

Subject: Request: mid-cycle capacity top-up and billing accelerator

Hi Rachel,

We're seeing a faster-than-expected ramp in inference usage for our patient triage workflows — looks like an immediate ~35% bump in monthly token consumption versus our forecast. We have some Qs before we commit to a larger uplift:

- Can Redwood provide a mid-cycle top-up that (a) adds committed capacity immediately and (b) smooths billing so it doesn't blow our Q1 forecast?
- We're also interested in an "accelerator" style credit (one-time) to offset the ramp if we sign an addendum now and annualize to our fiscal year end (12/31).

Attached our PO template and a short usage export. Would love a quick proposal and an estimate of timeline to turn this around — procurement prefers to avoid multiple amendments if possible.

Thanks,
Amelia Grant
Director, Platform Engineering
Clearview Health
[Attachment: Clearview_Topup_SOW_v1.pdf (PDF, 85KB)]

Date: 2027-02-20T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: mid-cycle capacity top-up and billing accelerator

Hi Amelia — thanks for the context and the export. Short answer: yes, we can do a mid-cycle top-up with a staged billing treatment plus a one-time accelerator credit tied to an annualization option.

I've looped in Ben (sales lead) and Lauren (billing/finance) to put concrete numbers behind this. High-level approach we typically use:

- Immediate committed top-up: provision X dedicated units on day 1 so latency/SLOs are preserved.
- Billing smoothing: prorate the added commitment over remaining term with an option to annualize the added dollars to your fiscal year-end.
- One-time accelerator credit: a capped credit applied to your next invoice if you sign the addendum within 10 business days.

If you can confirm the desired headroom (e.g., +35% vs current committed), we'll return a PDF SOW and a pricing spreadsheet with two options — standard top-up and top-up + annualize (with credit).

Ben/Lauren — can you take this and produce: (A) a draft addendum + SOW, (B) an accelerator-credit schedule (one-time dollar credit and conditions), and (C) the prorated billing math? Amelia indicated procurement prefers minimal amendments.

Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Rachel / Amelia. I'll draft two numbered pricing options here so it's easy for procurement to compare:

Option 1 — Rapid Top-up (minimal term change)\- Immediate add: +40% committed capacity (rounded)\- Effective immediately; prorated billing over remaining term (straight-line)\- No one-time credit\- List discount: 12% off incremental unit price

Option 2 — Accelerator Annualize (recommended if you expect sustained lift)\- Immediate add: +40% committed capacity\- Annualization: convert incremental add to an annualized commitment at next invoice cycle, aligned to 12/31 FY-end\- One-time accelerator credit: USD 25,000 applied against first two invoices post-addendum\- List discount: 18% off incremental unit price if signed within 10 business days

Notes:
- We can reduce the credit if you prefer a smaller initial credit in exchange for longer commit.
- We'll keep the original contract intact and append a single addendum (SOW + billing schedule).

I'll attach a pricing workbook and a redline-ready addendum for legal. Lauren — please confirm the prorate math and whether the credit requires a minimum invoice threshold.

Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_Midcycle_Pricing_Accelerator.xlsx (XLSX, 48KB)]

From: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
To: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com, Amelia Grant <amelia.grant@clearviewhealth.com>
Date: 2027-02-21T09:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: mid-cycle capacity top-up and billing accelerator

Hi all — quick clarification on billing mechanics and the credit:

- Proration: incremental committed units will be charged on a pro-rata basis for the remainder of the current term (based on days remaining). Example: if 180 days remain and you add $120k annualized equivalent, the prorated charge would be $60k for the remainder.
- Annualization path: if you elect the annualize option, we create an amendment that converts the prorated incremental add into a full-year commitment effective at the next billing cycle and align invoices to 12/31.
- Accelerator credit: the USD 25,000 credit will be treated as a one-time invoice credit and requires (a) execution of the addendum and (b) minimum incremental invoicing of USD 50k in the first 60 days post-addendum. If the threshold isn't met, the credit will be reduced pro rata.
- PO & SOW: procurement can send a PO referencing the addendum; we'll accept a PO that references the addendum number once signed. We can pre-fill the addendum SOW with the usage and units you provided.

I'll attach a quick pro-forma and a redline-friendly billing schedule.

Lauren Bishop
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Clearview_PO_Template.docx (DOCX, 12KB)]

If you can send the redline-ready addendum and the final pricing workbook by EOD, we will route for signature.
